newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslav army chief meets democracy campaigners.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslav army chief meets democracy campaigners.

text.p: Yugoslavia's army commander met Serbian pro-democracy demonstrators on Monday and indirectly voiced support for their campaign to restore opposition election victories annulled by the government.

An army statement said General Momcilo Perisic, chief of the general staff, told student activists he favoured a democratic solution to the crisis which has prompted weeks of demonstrations in Belgrade.

The opposition has won unprecedented expressions of solidarity from members of the Yugoslav establishment including army officers. The students obtained the meeting with Perisic on Monday to capitalise on sympathy for their cause.
Perisic stressed the army's non-involvement in politics but told the students he favoured a democratic solution that would help Yugoslavia rejoin Europe.

"In the course of the talks, General Perisic underlined the Yugoslav army's...special interest in seeing that all current problems are overcome within the legal institutions of the system in a manner deployed in democratic countries," said the statement released by the official news agency Tanjug.
It said such an approach was necessary to secure Yugoslavia's re-entry to the international community.
